Starting a new game. Initial checkpoint saved.

You see a gleaners' lined well.
A split in the fired lining lets the drawn water drain through the rim. Pack the gap with fire clay.
Repair: 2 fire clay. Composition: Masonry.

Fire clay seals this well's fired lining. A sound lining allows drinking and vessel filling; repairing a split takes two measures of fire clay. The old supply cellar in the western ruin stored repair clay. The reed basin nearby holds only a few drinks; it cannot refill this well.

A split in the fired lining lets the drawn water drain through the rim. Pack the gap with fire clay.

Frost creeps from the spine as you read. What is frozen is not armoured — it is brittle.
You drink. The well water is cool.

READER district-06-cellar-directions You see a gleaners' cellar tally.

Fire clay was kept in the far supply crate for the
well above. The broad passage is shortest, but
fresh marlback scratches cross it. A narrow service
passage turns north behind the wall. Its fallen
beam can be hauled from the western shoulder; the
winding passage beyond that shoulder stays open.
The stair returns to the glade. These marks promise
supplies, not safety.

READER district-08-supply-crate You see a gleaners' supply crate.

A shallow crate under an intact stretch of ceiling.
Wrapped fire clay was put aside for the broken
masonry well above; the remaining equipment belongs
to the abandoned store. Take only what you can
carry. Once emptied, the crate stays empty.
